utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-16-T, the Prosecutor versus Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Drago Josipovic, Dragan Papic, and Vladimir Santic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning. We may now resume the examination-in-chief of Mr. Vidovic. Counsel Radovic

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning. We ended yesterday with a question of how far, as the crow flies, your house was from the Kupreskic house, and you answered that question. I would now like to ask for a closed session for the next few questions. It will be a very brief session, but I am going to mention some names, so I don't want them publicly named.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Is private session okay instead of a closed session, so that we just shut off the sound?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Just without the sound.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be a private session then. (Private session)

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: (Open session)

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: You said that in the cultural and arts society, that you were a member of it until 1983; is that correct? Did it continue working after that date?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, but without the tambourine section.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, of all the members of the Kupreskic family that you see here, who continued working in that cultural and arts society?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: One of the first organisers, and an active member throughout its work, was Zoran Kupreskic and his brother Mirjan, and Vlatko was included in the work of the musical section from time to time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: We said yesterday that all the ethnicities, what was called the nations and nationalities of the region, were included in the cultural and arts society. Can you tell us something about whether, after the elections, attempts were made to break up that cultural and arts society and to form a single ethnicity society?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I know something about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Well, would you tell us and would you tell us what Zoran's attitude was towards attempts of this kind?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: After the elections, the initiative was launched to organise two cultural and arts societies. One of them was to be called Napredak, the Croatian society, Napredak meaning "Progress," and the second would be the Muslim society, called Proporod, "Rebirth." I know that at that time, Zoran, as one of the first coaches or trainers in the folklore section, together with his brother, always strove to have the cultural and arts society remain in the shape and form that it had always been and the composition that it had been up until then.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: What does that mean with regard to the membership and the ethnicity of the membership, the fact that he wanted the society to remain as it had always been?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, that meant that at that time there was a well tried and tested team.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Was it multi-national or uni-national?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, it was multi-nationality in composition. I'm going to try to enumerate some of the people who were the principal members of the society.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: The top team, Zoran Kupreskic; then we had Veljko Cato, Veljko Cato, he was a Serb by nationality; then there was Cengalovic, I don't know his name, that was his surname, he was a Romany; then there was the music sector with Fahrudin Ahmic; and, of course, there was Mirjan Kupreskic himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: You said that in 1993 you ceased working in the cultural and arts society. Did you, once you left this cultural and arts society, continue to be friends with Zoran Kupreskic?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: In 1983, I married, and in April 1994 (sic), I moved to Busovaca, so that my friendship with Zoran Kupreskic was more or less reduced to seeing him when I visited my parents during the weekend.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: I should like to ask for a correction in the transcript because the transcript states that he went to Busovaca in 1994 and he moved in 1984. The dates are 1984.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: When you returned during the weekends, did you meet, did you have a drink together and tell each other your news?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, very often, and we would go out often to have a good time together.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know, before the beginning of the war, on the 16th of April, when there was a joint performance staged by the cultural and arts society in the composition that Zoran wanted to have and that was in existence up until the war?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think that sometime in April, April 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: And what happened?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think that there was a holiday of some kind and some celebrations and performances within that scope.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: That brings us to your move to Busovaca where you got a flat. This was in 1984. Tell us when you returned to Vitez, please?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: You mean my job or when I got a flat there?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: I know that there is a difference there, so please tell us when you got a job and then afterwards when you got a flat. I apologise. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: When, in May 1989, I did an additional educational and training course, I returned to work in Vitez and began working at the post office there. There was a newly built telephone exchange of the AXE type, and I returned to live there, when I got a flat, on the 27th of July, 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: That was the time when you were given apartments to live in, they were socially-owned apartments given to staff, the staff; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. We exchanged one of these socially-owned flats that were given to the staff between Busovaca and Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, what extra training did you do for the new job?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: My additional training was training on the new telecommunications systems which were computer-directed, and I did this training in what was then the Nikola Tesla factory in Zagreb, and it is called Ericsson Nikola Tesla today.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: So your post office training was geared towards the technical side of the functioning of the post office or, more exactly, telecommunications within the postal service?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. My training was geared towards telecommunications and commutation systems, that is to say, exclusively telephone exchanges geared through computers, computerised.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: This brings us to 1990. Could you tell us about the events that took place prior to the free elections and what happened to the actual elections themselves and the electoral results, of course to the best of your knowledge, and what the power distribution was after the elections in the Vitez area?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: In 1990, in November, on the 18th of November, to be precise, multi-party elections were held. As far as I know, in connection with those elections, is that the initiative board and the president of that initiative board of the Croatian Democratic Community was one of my workers.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: His name was Franjo Kurevija. After the elections took place, there was a power division within the municipality, that is to say, executive power.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Before this division of power, after the free elections, tell me whether you had a role on the political scene? Did anything happen, was anything happening prior to the elections and the establishment of the HDZ in the post office itself?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, my role, that is to say, my support in this situation was -- actually, what I did was I gave my support to the president of the initiative board who spent most of his working time in political activities, and I would replace him -- I would leave him free to carry on with those political activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Before the elections, what was the national composition of the post office employees?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the Vitez post office, before the elections, of the 30 persons employed, six were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: I suppose that all the others were not all Croats. There were Serbs, were there not?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, there were two Serbs. And the rest -- that is to say, one Serb man and one Serb woman, and the others were Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Now, what happened with the power division after the elections?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: After the elections, as far as I know, of course, to the best of my knowledge, in the executive power of the municipality, in keeping with the electoral results, a joint body of power was constituted.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: How long did that joint body function?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, it functioned up until the end of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Was there not a division of the military component and the civilian component and the police component in that power structure?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: After the elections, a joint authority was set up in the police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: How long did it last, if you know that fact?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: You mean in the police?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the joint police station; how long did that go on for?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think that this went on until the end of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Your post office -- tell me, did every post office have a headquarters, that is to say, the telephone exchange, and did you cover an area including several post offices, and if you did, tell us all the post office exchanges that your headquarters and your post office exchange incorporated?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, it was the type of exchange that was installed in 1989, and this particular system was intended to cover the needs of telephone users in the whole municipality. When it was installed, there were two exchanges, telephone exchanges. They were the end terminals. One was installed at Poculica and the other in Stari Bila. Later on, there were plans for the construction of an underground network, and according to these new plans, the new telephone exchange would use state-of-the-art technology which would mean that the other two exchanges would be out of date, and the whole network would be built on the most modern techniques and would cater to the needs of the entire municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, did the network of users, up until the beginning of the war, yes, up until the outbreak of the war, did it have communication lines above ground or were you able to use an underground system exclusively?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: The network was actually a combined one, and this was reflected in the following: The underground network went until the settlement, and within the settlement, there was an aerial network.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, within your own telephone exchange, was it possible to establish, without going out to the ground, that there were any snags on the network, either aerial or underground?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That is the way the telephone exchange was conceived. It was computerised, and at any point in time, it could see what the situation was throughout the network with regard to all subscribers, except for these two networks that were all-type networks, that is to say, Stara Bila and all the subscribers who were linked to Stara Bila and Poculica and subscribers who were linked to Poculica and the other subscribers from other villages, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: So if I understood you correctly, within the telephone exchange, without actually going out to the ground, except for those places that you mentioned, you could actually establish for each and every subscriber whether his telephone was out of order or not? Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please describe this to us now, how you could ascertain, by way of computer, whether somebody's telephone had failed or was disconnected for one reason or the other because I imagine that you had data about each and every individual subscriber in your network. Could you please describe this to us?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: The telephone exchange was computerised, and that meant inter alia that there were two ways of monitoring the situation within the network. One is automatic, and the other is at the request of the operator, that is to say, that at a given point in time, the system automatically makes a printout of all the subscribers whose telephones are out of order, and this means that an alarm is sent to a certain post, either by way of light or sound.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: That is to say that the team for repairs goes out to the ground only when you receive this kind of alarm, and they know exactly where to go; right?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes, and if you allow me to continue, the other way of doing it is at the request of the operator.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: How does the operator get this information?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: There is a command that is issued to the computer to print out at a given point in time all the subscription numbers that are out of order at that given point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: All right. We will go back to the system later when we start dealing with the 16th of April. Tell me, you were born in Pirici, and that's where your family house was or, rather, the house that you were born in. In the meantime, you got a flat of your own and you lived there. Didn't you want to have a house of your own in the village where you were born?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I did have that kind of a wish, and I managed to carry it through.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Can I hear about this now? When did you start fulfilling this wish of yours?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I started building my house in '84/'85. Perhaps 1985 would be more accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: When did you finish it, or did you complete it before the war?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I managed to put a roof on it in 1991, at the very end of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Did you stop with your building then?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I ran out of money.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Did you obtain any materials before the war?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. In addition to the construction materials that were needed to cover the house with a roof, I also got some of the wood needed for windows. I also got some wooden boards and some other materials that remained piled up within the house in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, after the free elections, were you involved anywhere from a political point of view?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: After the elections in 1990, I was not politically involved, except for supporting a party.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Which party?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: The Croatian Democratic Community. I also supported my colleagues at work, and I mentioned a few minutes ago who these people were.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you something else in relation to military service. Tell me, when you left the JNA, did you apply to the military department or whatever it was called in those days?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Yes, I did. That was my obligation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, did you get any kind of war assignment?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Where and what?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: In 1981, it was in the military post office in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: What was your specialty?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: My specialty was communications, teleprinter communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, when you became the technical director, that's a word we're all going to understand, of the post office in Vitez, did you get a war assignment within that post office or did you get work duty within the post office? Is that what we're going to call it now?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: When I started working in Busovaca, at the request of my directorate, my war assignment was changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: From 1982 onwards, my military assignment was by way of work duty at the post office in Busovaca where I worked. To the best of my understanding, you got a war assignment for a civilian post.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: That is to say, within the post office?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: You were basically the only technical expert for telecommunications; did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Now, could you please tell me something about telephone connections. Just before the war or in 1992, telephone traffic, in terms of the military and the civilian, were they one or were they separated?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: These were separate systems.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: That is to say, within the post office, there were no military connections; did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, not before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Except for certain telephones, for example, those who belonged to the civilian network, more or less?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: You mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: I mean --

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes, they used automatic telephone numbers, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, that's what I was referring to. These are not special military telephones. It's just like any other telephone; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: While you worked at the post office in Vitez, did you hear about an event that occurred on the 20th of October, 1992 by the cemetery in Ahmici or, rather, the cemetery to which the late Hazim had given part of his land, sold part of his land? So if you did hear something about this, could you tell us what you heard about this?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear something about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: But you were not a direct participant?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I was not a direct participant. I only heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: So what did you hear?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 20th of October, a group of locals from Ahmici, that's what I heard, put up a roadblock by the cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: What kind of a group, Croats or Muslims?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: A group of Muslims from Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear how this was settled?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know the details, how this was worked out, but I do know that this misunderstanding lasted one day, an entire day, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, after the free elections within the post office, in terms of what you did yourself and what you observed by yourself, rather than through what you heard from other persons, was the ethnic composition of the employees at the post office changed?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: But you would have to know, wouldn't you? You were the boss there; right?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I understood your question, but you talked about the entire enterprise, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm asking you only about the post office because I'm talking about your very own observations. I'm talking about the post office where you actually worked.

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the post office, there were no changes in the ethnic composition. The way it was before the elections is the way it remained.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, were there any problems in terms of the Muslims coming to work after that, shall we call it, incident on the 20th of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. They did not come to work for seven days, and I don't know why.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: After those seven days?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: After those seven days, they showed up.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, were any disciplinary measures taken against them because they failed to show up for work for seven days?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, no. No disciplinary action was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Did they explain at all why they didn't come to work?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, they did. They said that they were afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: And you were satisfied with that kind of an explanation?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, our explanation was that there was no need to be afraid because the post office worked throughout this period. It was a public institution, and every day, about 200 people go through the post office, different clients. So our answer was that there was no need to be afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, the Muslim employees of the post office, how long did they work at the post office actually?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: They worked until the 15th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, do you recall that day, the 15th of April, 1993? That was the day before the outbreak of the war between the Croats and the Muslims. Do you remember what you did on that day?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do. On the 15th of April and a few days before that, my activities were reduced to buying oil and gasoline for the aggregates, because at that time, there were power blackouts quite often, and this was one of my regular duties, that I had to provide for fuel several times during the month. On that day, the 15th, I managed to get an additional quantity, about 400 litres of oil, and I worked until 3.00, and then I went home.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember where you obtained this last quantity of oil?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I got it at the gasoline station Kalem, at Kasim Kresic's.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: That's a Muslim, judging by his name and surname; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: After you went home, what did you do on the 15th of April? Did you go back to the post office?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Those days when there were these regular power blackouts, we had organised duty in the post office, and the only task involved was to turn on the aggregate if there was a power shortage.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know in advance who would be on duty when?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Were Muslims on duty too?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Now, tell us what happened. You went out there on duty, and was this round-the-clock duty? Did people come during the night too? How did you organise this?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. This duty started from 8.00 p.m. and it went on until 7.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: I imagine that 7.00 a.m. is the time when all other employees would come to work; right?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, what were the conditions for duty at the post office? Was there a bed where people could take a nap? Did they have to sit there? I mean, what would they do if an alarm didn't go off?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: The conditions were very good. We had a bed just below the alarm board, and if any kind of alarm went off, just as when there would be a power cut, the alarm would go off, sound and light, I mean, and the alarm was so loud that it could wake up anyone, even people who were fast asleep. So the person who was on duty was supposed to turn on the aggregate and then switch it off when electricity was restored.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: All right. So we talked about the 15th of April, and we shall talk about the 16th later. Just tell me, do you know something about village guards in Ahmici, Pirici? Were they joint guards or separate guards?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know that in the entire municipality, everywhere, there were village guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: And how they were organised?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: That, I do not know. I'm not aware of that. I did not have any insight into this.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: So you did not know whether they were linked up horizontally or vertically?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: That, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that the Muslims had their own village guard?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, did you hear about a specific group of armed Muslims? Did anyone see them going out for some kind of exercise? I mean, you know what you heard. I don't know what you heard. You do.

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear something.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: My sister met a large group of armed Muslim neighbours led by Fuad Berbic. The group was, as she explained it to me, the group were marching, actually, she said they were marching. I don't know whether I have used the correct term.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: You're close to it.

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: So they marched by her and said hello, and Fuad said, "You shouldn't be afraid, neighbour. This is only a drill." She knew all the members of that group.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us when your sister told you of this? What date was that? When she saw it or when she told you of the incident, when she told you about it and when she had actually seen it happen?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was somewhere towards the end of 1992, sometime in November.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: That she told you about this incident?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, she told me several days later, and she said, "Several days ago, I saw the following." That was how it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us your sister's name?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: My sister's name is Gordana Vidovic. She is married and her married surname is Suic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Has she always been called to the Tribunal to testify?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think she has been called, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me now, the 16th of April, you were to be in the post office by 7.00 a.m., if I understood you correctly.

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: When did you notice that something was happening?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Every morning at 7.00 a.m., the automatised system would print out the alarm list. On that alarm list, as far as the breakdowns were concerned, there was nothing to report.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: This was 7.00 a.m.; right?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. It was only at my own request as the operator, sometime around 7.30 or 8.00, we had a long list of subscriber and telephone numbers that were out of order.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any information as to what had happened, why they were out of order?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I did not have any information on this, but as I heard shooting, which woke we up at 6.00, I was able to assume what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, apart from noticing what was happening on the apparatus, on the device, that there was trouble, did you exclude anybody on this particular date although their telephone lines were in order? Did you disconnect anyone?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: On that day, we did not, because until the end of the day, I was not physically able to divide up the people whose telephone numbers were out of order because there were more and more people who had telephones out of order.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Where was your mother on the 16th of April? Where did she live?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, my mother and my sister lived in her own house down below.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Did she have a telephone in her house?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, she did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Weren't you interested in what was happening to her? Did you call her up to say, "Mommy, are you alive and well? What's happening? What's going on there?"

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, on the printout list, I saw that my mother's number, telephone number, was on that list, and, of course I was interested in learning what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: So what did you undertake?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that moment, all the other neighbours who were not on the list, I would check their telephones and see where she was, and on that same day, sometime after noon, I learnt that she was in Zume in a shelter there, in the basement of a house belonging to Jozo Vrebac, a cousin.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Did you learn this directly from your mother, in talking to her, or from a neighbour?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I learned this from Mrs. Ljuba Vidovic, who is the next-door neighbour to the house where the shelter was located.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, did Ljuba Vidovic tell you what was going on?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, she did, more or less. She said that my mother and my sister and many other women had been put up in the shelter there, and any other details, I don't know about, apart from the fact that there was shooting going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, on the 16th of April, were the telephones cut in Stari Vitez, the Muslim part?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Were the telephone links with Stari Vitez cut at any time during this troubled period?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, on the second or third day after the 16th of April, we cut off a cable, the telephone cable in Stari Vitez, which fed all the subscribers, telephone subscribers, in Stari Vitez, upper and lower Veceriska, Krcevine, Jardol, Divjak, and the surrounding villages moving up towards Stara Bila.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: So this cable-cutting, was this done by the Croats or the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: We -- that is to say, on the second, the instrument that we had in our possession, were able to ascertain the location at which the cable was cut, the exact distance and point where the cable was cut, and the location was in a concrete grid below -- across the road from the house of Enes Sehic in Stari Vitez, and that was exclusively a Muslim populated area.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Later on, were you able to ascertain physically, that is to say, did you go and see this for yourself, or your workers, to see the position where the cutoff took place and whether there was just one place that the cable was cut or several places?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: After the war in 1994, when we started to repair the cables, the main cables, we found the exact place in Stari Vitez where the cable had been cut and the method in which the cable had been cut, not only in that particular concrete slab but at seven other points.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Were you able to say what the cable had been cut with, the instrument used?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. In this concrete slab where the cable was fitted, it was a special metal-cutting device that was used, and on other places, a crimp or some other sharp instrument.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: How was this communication line set up after that? Did you replace the cable itself or did you do anything else?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, at all these points where the cable was cut, together with AMG, support from AMG, and the technical cables and links, we were able to link up and use what we popularly refer to as a bypass, we bypassed the cables, linked them up together again, and this was done in May 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: When the war broke out, on the premises of the post office building in the basement, was the wartime government, or whatever it was called, stationed in that basement?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, because I suppose the post office was the sole building in Vitez which had an additional power supply system, and, of course, a basement is always a safe place; and in the basement of the post office was the system for information, 985.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, on the 15th of April, did you watch television? Did you watch the news?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Did any of the people that you contacted, that you met that day, did they tell you that there were some items of special interest broadcast on the news that day?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear anything like that from anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear about the case of Zivko Totic and the death of the person accompanying him on the 15th of April?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I heard about this incident on the 18th or 19th, what happened in Zenica, but not on that particular day, on the 15th.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know the fact that there had been previous incidents with casualties and that the incidents were caused by the Muslim side?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear of things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: What did you hear?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I heard that there were incidents in Gornji Vakuf and in Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: What were those incidents? What did they consist of? What happened? Tell me what you heard.

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, this is what I heard. What happened was that some people were arrested, were detained, people who were -- I don't know how to express myself -- who were interesting for the Muslims, whom the Muslims had an interest in. In other words, those who had already become involved in questions of defence or some other political activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, after the 16th or during the 16th, did you hear what had happened in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. On the 16th, in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: What did you hear?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I heard that in Ahmici, there was a very strong conflict on that particular day, the 16th.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: What were the results of that conflict? Did you hear anything about that?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I heard that the results were that there were a lot of dead on both sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Can you quote the figures? Did you hear how many had died on the Muslim side and how many people had been killed on the Croat side?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear anything about the figures on that day, just that there were casualties.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, did you hear, on the Croatian side, which individuals died, from which units, the members of which units?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I heard that Mirjan Santic had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: What unit did he belong to?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know. He is from the neighbouring village. I knew him, but I don't know which unit he belonged to or whether, in fact, he belonged to any unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell us whether you know anything about the fact that after the 16th or during the 16th the Muslim population was taken away to certain centres and buildings, such as the cinema, the basement of the cinema, in actual fact?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that a group was in the cinema, but I don't know whether in the basement.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know how they were liberated, freed?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know. I suppose that there was an exchange of some kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell us about your political or military role. Did you have any political or military role, or did you only perform your work assignments in the post office?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: My role was exclusively reflected in my work duties at the telephone exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you knew Zoran Kupreskic very well; did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think we need to have character witnesses later on when we have a witness here who knows him, so I'm going to ask him directly ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain the character of Zoran Kupreskic, his basic features?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I have known Zoran since he was a boy. I have known him as long as I know myself. We grew up together. We went to the same class at school for eight years. His character, I can say, was similar to my own, and I could describe it in the following way: He liked his friends a lot. He, even when we were small children or when we were growing up, he was not a difficult person or bad-tempered. I don't know which term to use exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Was he prone to fights or brawls of any kind?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. He was -- he had a competitive spirit and we always competed amongst ourselves in our learning abilities and who would do best in school and have top marks and get a 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Shall we explain to the Trial Chamber that a 5 is the top mark given to pupils in our schools?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes. We were excellent pupils, both of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: What happened later on with him? How did his life progress?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, he -- when he completed school in Novi Travnik, the machine technology sector, and later on went to the faculty, machine faculty, building faculty in Zenica, and he was of a very firm character, an upright character, an individual who saw his life based on the work he did, hard work.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: What did he do outside the school and outside his education and work?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, he played music and he worked in folklore, folklore was a hobby of his, and this meant that he was very sociable, and he has this facility of being very sociable and he has a very positive outlook toward his friends, and it is common knowledge that in the folklore sector, as a coach or trainer, that people probably liked him best.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: How would you describe Mirjan Kupreskic?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mirjan was younger, a few years younger, so that the -- his early days -- I don't know -- I didn't know him as well as I did Zoran when we were children because he was younger, but when he grew up, he had exactly the same characteristics and likes and affinities as Zoran did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Were they respected in their working environment and in the community in general?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, they were, both in their working environment and in the village and throughout Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Only with the Croatian community or with others as well?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: By everybody. He was generally respected.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, since you have given such a characterisation of them, do you think that it is possible that they would have killed someone, torched his house, killed his children, things like that?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. No, no. Not even in my subconscious could I dream of anything like it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Counsel Radovic. Does any Defence counsel intend to cross-examine -- examination-in-chief. Yes. Counsel Slokovic-Glumac.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. Vidovic, just a few questions. You said that on the 20th of October, 1992, the Muslims did not show up for work at the post office; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Tell me, do you know, according to the law that was in force at that time, did an absence of over five days from work have any consequences?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The consequence being that one would lose one's job.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Were any proceedings initiated against these persons to have their jobs taken away from them?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Who was your deputy at the post office?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: My deputy was Asim Arnautovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: What was Asim Arnautovic?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was a telecommunications engineer by profession.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: And by ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: By ethnicity, he's a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, since you had to be in touch with other companies in Vitez and you probably knew the situation there, was the structure of employees or of the management changed in any company in Vitez in '92, in '93, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, there were no changes anywhere, either in terms of management or in terms of the general employment pattern.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: The post office is one of the companies that was a public company. Those are so-called public companies; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: And it is under state control in a certain sense?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: At any point in time after the elections and until the outbreak of the war, were any attempts made or were any initiatives launched from any side in the municipality that people had to sign an allegiance of loyalty to the HVO?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, no, there were no such attempts. At least I don't know about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you something in relation to Ahmici. Your mother and your sister live there, is that correct, and your brother too?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Where was your brother in 1992 and 1993? What was his name, please?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: My brother's name is Mirko Vidovic, and he was in Ahmici or, rather, Pirici until the second half of March 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Where did he go to then and where was his family at the time?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the first half of 1992, his wife and two children went to stay with her mother in Germany.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Why did they go?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, at the time, they were probably afraid, right? They were afraid of an aggression by the Serb army or somebody else. I don't know. I know that that was approximately the reason why his wife and two children had left.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: He left in 1993, in mid March; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes, and he went to pick them up, and he didn't manage to come back until 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Was your brother friends with Mirjan Kupreskic? Were they on duty together in '92 and '93? Did you know about this? Did you discuss it? Of course, if you know about it.

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes, they were very good friends, and they visited one another, and I think they were also on duty together.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: You said that you intervened or, rather, tried to get in touch with your mother on the 16th of April so that you would find out where she was. Did you sometimes check on where your sister was, where your mother was? Did you talk about the situation in Vitez, things like that? Were there any situations before this that made you feel anxious in any way, and did you feel wary in terms of something happening? Did you want to get them out?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I was very often in contact with my mother and with my sister whenever something happened, even in the broader region, because they lived on their own, and I was simply afraid for them. Very often, I would caution them, saying that if they felt anything, that they should go up to the Kupreskic houses, any one of the Kupreskic houses, because I think that they would spend the night safer there than in their own home.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Do you know whether Fahrudin Ahmic was friends with Zoran and Mirjan Kupreskic? I'm talking about the Fahrudin Ahmic who played an instrument in that society.

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I know that they were very good friends, and for many years, they played instruments together and stayed in the cultural society.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Do you know whether he remained with them as a member of this society until the outbreak of the war?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, certainly until the outbreak of the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear Zoran or Mirjan Kupreskic expressing any kind of extremist views?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, no, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Were they involved in any kind of political activity?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think that Zoran was, for a brief period, in the local community together with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Possibly in 1980, 1981 or, rather, 1981, 1982.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Was he a member of the League of Communists, since you say that he was active in the local community at that time?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes, he was a member of the League of Communists.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Do you know whether they were active after the elections, either one or the other?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, no, I don't think that either one of them was.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear them support any extremist views on the Croatian side in any conversation? Did you ever hear anything of that nature? Were you ever present?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I never heard them present any such views in favour of the extremist side.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Counsel Slokovic-Glumac. Does any Defence counsel intend to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Good day, Your Honours. I would like to inform you that Borislav Krajina, Luka Susak, and Petar Puliselic will also be examining this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel Krajina?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Good day, Mr. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: My name is Borislav Krajina. I'm Defence counsel for Vlatko Kupreskic, the accused. I would like to put a few questions to you. First of all, you mentioned a few minutes ago in your statement that your brother, Mirko Vidovic, left the area of the municipality of Vitez in the second half of March 1993 and that he went to Germany to collect his family and that he managed to return only in 1994; is that correct? Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Please, in this connection, can you tell me with certainty, can you answer with certainty, whether your brother, Mirko Vidovic, was in Ahmici and in Pirici on the 15th of April, 1993, that is to say, a day before the conflict broke out?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, no, no. He was in Germany. I'm sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Thank you. Also, I wish to ask you the following: Do you know Vlatko Kupreskic? Do you see him in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do. I grew up together with him too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us how long you've known Vlatko Kupreskic and what is this based upon? You said that you grew up together. Are you neighbours? Did you, perhaps, work together? Were you schoolmates? Could you tell us about this a bit?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I've known Vlatko and Zoran for as long as I've known myself. We grew up together, and we were friends from early childhood. When we grew up too, very often, for as long as I lived there, we saw each other, and later on too, although rarely, I must say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: All right. Can you tell us now what schools Vlatko Kupreskic finished? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do. After elementary school, he completed a vocational school in Travnik for economics, and after that, he graduated from the Faculty of Economics in Zenica. He got a university degree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Do you know whether Vlatko Kupreskic, just before the war and then during the war and after the war, was he ever involved in politics? Do you know about it?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, never, not before the war, not after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: All right. Do you know whether he spoke publicly at political gatherings or something?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, never, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Do you know what were the things that he basically did at the time?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I know. Before he established a private company, a trading company, in addition to the regular job he had at the Vitezit factory, Vlatko played an instrument, and he played at restaurants, hotels, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Tell me, do you know whether Vlatko Kupreskic did his military service?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know he did not do his military service. Because of his health, he was incapable of doing his military service.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Did you ever see him in a military uniform or with weapons?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, never, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Do you know whether Vlatko Kupreskic is a heart patient?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I remember when we were seeing him off when he was going to have heart surgery, we were in the second grade of primary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: All right. You said that you grew up in Pirici, et cetera. Did you have Muslims amongst your neighbours?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Do you know what kind of attitude Vlatko Kupreskic had towards his neighbours and Muslims, do you know about that, before the war, during the war, after the war?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do know about it. He had a good relationship. Very often, he would go and play his instrument at various neighbours' places in Ahmici when they were sending off their men to the army, Muharem Patkovic, to mention a few names, when he was going into the army, and then Berbic, I don't know his first name, et cetera. I think that also his positive attitude was expressed through Veleprodaja, that is to say, his shop. He built this building of Veleprodaja, and some of them found jobs at his place, for example, Hazim Ahmic from Gornji Pirici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: All right. Just one more thing, one more question: Since you said that you grew up together and you knew Vlatko Kupreskic very well, could you tell us now at the end something about Vlatko as a person, what kind of a person he was like as a child, as he was growing up, as an adult? Could you tell us something about his character and what kind of reputation he enjoyed in your environment?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Excuse me. I'm going to say something similar to what I have already said about Zoran. When we were young, all of us were schoolmates together, and we were competitive, and we were competing as to who would be more successful in life. Every one of us had an objective in life. We wanted to complete our education and to provide for ourselves and for our families properly. I think that this is a characteristic of good men, and in that sense, I think that that is the kind of assessment one can give of Vlatko's character too. As we were growing up, if we're talking about his relationship with friends and colleagues, he really knew how to create a good atmosphere. That is what we always say. He can entertain very well, and I already said that he spent part of his working career by entertaining others.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Did he ever have any inclination towards excessive behaviour or aggressive behaviour of any kind?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, no, to the best of my knowledge, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vidovic. Thank you, Mr. President. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel Susak?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Vidovic. I am the Defence counsel for Drago Josipovic. My name is Luka Susak, and I'm going to ask you a few questions. You said that you were from Pirici. Do you know the Vjetrenica company of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know that it exists? Did they have a warehouse in Santici?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: The warehouse is named Ogrjev, and the address is Santici BB, with that number. Can you describe to us the locality of that warehouse? Where is it located?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I can. The warehouse is located along the main road between the railway station in Vitez and Kaonik or, to be more precise, between Pican's cafe and the road leading to Ahmici and Pirici.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So it is the main road and the section between Travnik and Kaonik; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Would you describe to us, please, whether there is a fence around the warehouse of any kind?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, there is, right around the whole warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you tell us what kind of fence it is? Is it a concrete wall or a steel fence or a wire fence or anything else?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, the fence is made up of concrete slabs, supports, and on these concrete supports, there is wiring attached.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What about this wiring, has it got any sort of fields in between?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What dimensions are the holes in between?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, they are approximately square shaped, and let us say they are 20 centimetres by 20 or 15 by 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Now, my next question: Can you climb up the fence, as you would up a ladder, in view of the profile of the wire itself?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, you can climb up this type of concrete wire fencing, just as you would up a ladder.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Now, we looked at aerial photographs here, and we know the entrance, the door, leading into the warehouse, and there was a certain amount of misunderstanding on that point, so I ask you my next question: This entrance door into the warehouse courtyard, is the door placed on the side of the main road or somewhere else? That is to say, is the entrance door on the main road or on the other side of the road?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: The entrance to Ogrjev is not on the side of the main road, it is on the parking lot side, that is to say, the lateral side of Ogrjev.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So it is on the lateral side and not the main road side?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: At the entrance, has the door got one side to it or is it a double door?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think that there are two sides to the door, a big one and a small one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What is the big side used for and what about the small side and are they linked together, as you remember the entrance?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: The big entrance is closed unless somebody needs to take out some materials. Usually people coming to Ogrjev would park their vehicles in the parking lot and would then enter the Ogrjev premises through the small door by foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So as far as I'm able to conclude, the vehicles enter through the big entrance, the big door, which is kept locked, to take material out of Ogrjev and big material into Ogrjev; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know the guardhouse in the compound?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. In one corner, there was a small hut for the guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What do you mean by a hut?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: A small house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Is it several-storeyed or just a ground-floor building?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: It's on the ground floor. And when I say "small," I mean of small dimension.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Well, has it got an entrance door and any windows?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it has a door and windows.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Are the windows glassed in? Is there any glass on the windows, or what do these apertures look like?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, they're classical windows with glass.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: While we are on the subject of windows, you know what the west side is and what the northerly side is. Are the windows on just one side or on several sides of this guard house?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I'm sure it has a window looking out towards the west and south, facing west and facing south.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Susak, I assume you have a few more questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Yes, there will be questions to the tune of ten to fifteen minutes, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We will have a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: --- Upon resuming at 11.05 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, Counsel Pavkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the defence would like to make an objection with regard to procedure on the part of the Prosecutor because two or three minutes before you walked in we received this batch of material. If only a part of these documents will be the subject of the cross-examination by the Prosecution, then we should like to raise an objection, because the defence was not able to nor can it objectively prepare itself and become informed of what these documents state, even partially. So I should like to ask you to bear this in mind. Apart from that the photocopies are very bad and are not legible in many places. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Terrier?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I simply wish to make one comment. It is not our intention to use one of these documents in the cross-examination of this witness. However, we reserve the possibility of using one or more of these documents during the cross-examination of others. This is merely -- we're merely giving the opportunity to the defence to have the documents that we have selected and decided to disclose to the Defence. With regards to the poor quality of the photocopies of these documents, as Mr. Pavkovic has just mentioned, I admit that this is indeed the case, but we will try to do what we can to improve upon them, but I'm sorry for the time being we cannot give them better quality copies. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Very well. No problem there. Counsel Susak?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: We stopped at Ogrjev, Mr. Vidovic; we were discussing Ogrjev. The western part, you said that the window faced west in the guardhouse, and that there was a south facing window, and that both the windows had glass. What direction did the window facing west look out on to?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: What do you mean, what direction?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: In what direction: If you were to look through the window facing west of the guardhouse, what would you see through that window?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, you would see Vitez. You would be looking in the direction of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What about the south side, the south window?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: The south window looks out on to the main road from Travnik to Kaonik.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Which houses are near the window facing west? That is to say, near the warehouse belonging to Ogrjev?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: There we have the house of -- the closest house is -- belongs to Avdo Becirevic. We called him -- Mujaga's son-in-law; I think his surname was Becirevic, though. And behind his house is Mura Dzidic's house. Further on upwards, you come to Sefik Pezer's house, and to the right of Mura Dzidic is the house belonging to Mehmed Ahmic, and further on towards the right you have Smail Ahmic's house, and below his house is his son's house, Mujo Ahmic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: The houses that you have just enumerated and their owners, are they all Muslims?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, they are. They're all Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So the window facing west of the guardhouse is turned towards houses belonging to Muslims; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Can we say that they are exclusively Muslim-owned houses?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, right up by the Ogrjev company are houses belonging exclusively to Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: On the west side over the fence, that is to say, could you come out on to the macadamised road surface from the western side?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, you could cross over the fence just as you would climb up a ladder and cross on to the other side, on any of the sides surrounding the compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you tell us now please whether from the angle of the guardhouse, that is between the guardhouse and the steel fence, can you see the south side -- that is part of Santici across from the main road?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, not all of it. You can see a part of it, but not the entire area.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Would you tell us where Drago Santic's house is located? Is it across the main road, or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Drago Santic?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: No, Drago Josipovic. I apologise for that slip.

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Drago Josipovic's house is situated opposite to Ogrjev; in other words, on the right-hand side of the main road running from Travnik to Kaonik.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Is it on the -- to the southerly side of the guardhouse?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, to the south side of the guardhouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Can you tell us which houses surround Drago Josipovic's house, and whether near his house there are any Muslim-owned houses? Or let me add to that, could you tell us the distribution of the houses bordering on Drago Josipovic's house?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Very well. To the west of Drago Josipovic's house, at a distance of 30 metres, is his parents' house and his brother's house, Miro right behind that house, behind his parents' house and Miro's house, is, at a distance of 5 metres, the house of Hasim Ahmic. And right next to that house, on the south side, therefore on the south side of Hasim Ahmic's house, we have very close by, 5 or 6 metres away, his son's house, Fahrudin, or Fahran, as we used to call him, Ahmic. On the east --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Susak, do you intend to pursue this line of questioning? Because we have aerial photographs of the whole place. We know everything about the location of the various houses. Is it necessary for the witness to tell us where the various houses are located? I'm just wondering.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, yes, we do know where the houses are located, but we are ascertaining who the owners are, and that is why I'm asking these questions because the witnesses for the Prosecution said something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: No, that's right, we know that as well. We know that as well, the owners of the various houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, but I've almost concluded, just to give us a general idea, a general picture. We'll be finished in just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you enumerate the houses situated to the east of the facility owned by Drago Josipovic. To the east of -- yes, you said Ivica's or Miro's house, Hasim Ahmic's house and Fahrudin Ahmic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Now on the other side, what do we have there?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: To the east of Drago Josipovic's house, at a distance of 50 metres, lies Jozo Santic's house. Also on the east, below Jozo Santic's house, we have Vlado Santic's house, Jozo's son's house. There's another house there which is empty, I think; nobody lives there. But I think the owner is a cousin of the Santics, and I don't think it is furnished, either.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: How far are these houses from Drago Josipovic's house?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So that means that they are further away than the houses owned by the Muslims, as far as I was able to gather?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did you know Drago Josipovic previously?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Would you tell us, you delved in politics; was he active in politics, did he take part in any power structures in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I've known Drago since we were children, and he never had anything to do with politics.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know what his conduct was towards his neighbours, how did he behave towards his Muslim neighbours?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, they were good relations, very good. Their relations were particularly good with neighbours to the west, that is to say Hasim and his sons.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know whether Drago Josipovic ever did any excessive behaviour, or made any criminal offence or anything?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No as far as I know, he did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know where he worked?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do. He worked in the SPS factory, the Sintevit section for plastics, I think Sintevit was the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was he a sportsman in Ahmici or Santici? Did he take part in any sports of any kind?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Not to any great extent, but he was a sympathiser and was on the board of the football club and team at one point, the football club that existed and was called the NK Santic football club.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was he respected in his environment and in Santici as a whole?

utterances.speaker: Rudo Vidovic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Drago is a quiet man by nature. And as such, he was respected.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Counsel Susak. Counsel Puliselic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
